title: Blakey's advice to turn a mistake into something
summary: On 'feature time' Jackson kept going back to fix phrases, and Blakey told him to make a mistake loud and move on.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Can you give me a specific example of something he might have done for taking care of business on the bandstand for instance?

On the bandstand it wasn’t so authoritative as opposed to maybe some general situations. I mean travel decisions had to be made. On the bandstand Art was supportive. Now for example if there was something that he didn’t like he wouldn’t tell you what to do, but he would say leave that aspect out. For example, one time I was at a part of a show called “feature time” where he would let an artist come down front and play a ballad feature with the rhythm section. So I’m the saxophonist, piano, bass and Art, and I play a ballad. So just joining, sometimes we’re working on these figures or working on lines on our own, for phrases. And I had a bit of a habit with playing a phrase, maybe the phrase didn’t come out like I wanted, and maybe going back and trying to play the phrase, okay? And a couple of times I think maybe I was doing it in a way that it was noticeable to the audience so he just said, “Listen, you make a mistake, make it loud but move on, you don’t have to go back. Turn the mistake into something.” So in that way he told me what not to do but he encouraged me and supported me to make the mistake, something that everyone would appreciate anyway and no one is going to notice a mistake unless you basically say oh I’m sorry, I’d better do that one again, which is basically what I said, through the saxophone. So if that gives you an idea of the kind of person that he was, and he was really supportive. And again, I don’t ever remember him telling someone what to do, but he would say, “Leave that out,” or, “don’t do that one again.” And obviously the verbiage would be a little different than I’m using now but you get the gist of what I’m trying to say.
